subject: Banking
title: The Shrinking Role of Cash
description: One-minute skill: The Shrinking Role of Cash.

hook.text: Sweden is 98% cashless. Cash use has fallen below 1% of transactions.

buildup.text: Digital payments are faster, trackable, and cheaper. Businesses prefer cards because cash handling costs 1-2% of sales.

discovery.text: As cash disappears, central banks lose a direct connection to citizens.

twist.text: Cashless societies exclude the unbanked. 4.5% of US households have no bank account.

climax.text: Cash is freedom from surveillance and banking requirements.

punchline.text: 98% cashless in Sweden. But 4.5% of Americans have no bank account.

quiz.question: What percentage of transactions in Sweden use cash?

details.summary: Physical cash use is declining rapidly worldwide as digital payments dominate, forcing central banks to consider what happens when their most visible product becomes obsolete and the private sector controls all payment infrastructure.
details.whyItMatters: Cash is the only form of money directly issued by the central bank to citizens. As it disappears, the public's direct connection to public money is severed, raising questions about monetary sovereignty and financial inclusion.
takeaways: Sweden's cash use has dropped below 10 percent of transactions
Cash disappearance could exclude the elderly and unbanked from the economy
CBDCs are partly motivated by the desire to maintain public money access

faq.question: What happens if cash disappears completely?
faq.answer: All transactions would flow through private banks and payment companies, giving them enormous power. People without bank accounts or digital access would be excluded from the economy. Central banks would lose their direct connection to citizens.

faq.question: Are any countries pushing back against going cashless?
faq.answer: Several countries have passed or proposed laws requiring businesses to accept cash. The EU is working on legislation guaranteeing cash acceptance. These efforts aim to preserve financial inclusion and prevent total private sector control of payments.
